documents.title: Postgres connection pool runbook
documents.text: When PostgreSQL reports remaining connection slots are reserved, inspect the total pool budget. Sum replicas multiplied by DB_POOL_SIZE and reserve headroom for migrations and administration. checkout-api uses 8 replicas and the database permits 200 connections. A pool of 10 per replica uses 80 slots; 50 per replica requests 400. Restore the previous pool configuration or roll back the release, then check error rate and active connections. Do not increase max_connections without reviewing memory limits.

documents.title: Checkout deployment checklist
documents.text: Before releasing checkout-api, validate database connectivity, execute a test payment, and inspect the configured DB_POOL_SIZE. Rollback requires operator approval. After rollback, compare 5xx rate and successful payment rate against the pre-release baseline. A rollback can mitigate an incident without proving its root cause.

documents.title: Previous incident: connection saturation
documents.text: A previous staging incident exhausted database connections after increasing worker replicas. The error was remaining connection slots are reserved. Reducing the aggregate connection pool restored availability. Verify all connection consumers when diagnosing a recurrence.

documents.title: Inventory API rate-limit runbook
documents.text: If inventory-api returns 429 with Retry-After, honor the delay and use exponential backoff with jitter. Zero-delay retries can amplify throttling and grow the orders queue. Restore RETRY_BACKOFF_MS to at least 1000, review retry limits, and observe queue drain. Do not add workers while the dependency is throttling.

documents.title: Orders queue recovery
documents.text: When queue depth rises, compare worker throughput, retry rate, and downstream errors. A growing queue alone does not establish a cause. Check retry configuration after a deployment. Roll back only after operator approval and verify jobs are idempotent before reprocessing.

documents.title: Search latency investigation
documents.text: High search latency has multiple possible causes: index changes, cache misses, query volume, or downstream failures. Collect traces, query timings, cache hit rate, and recent deploy metadata. Without these signals, report insufficient evidence rather than choosing a cause. Compare p95 latency with the 500ms SLO.

report.headline: Connection pool budget exceeds database capacity
report.summary: The release raised the per-replica pool to 50. Across 8 replicas that requests 400 connections against a 200-connection database limit. Captured logs show connection exhaustion. This is a supported hypothesis; mitigation still needs verification.

findings.text: The rollout changed DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 50 on 8 replicas.
PostgreSQL is rejecting connections at its 200-connection limit.
The requested connection budget is 400; the previous configuration requested 80.

steps: Restore DB_POOL_SIZE=10 or roll back to v2.7.4.
Observe database connections and checkout 5xx rate.
Confirm successful test payments before resolving the incident.
